policy: Version = `<ponder-version>-sqd.<rev>`: @subsquid/ponder@X.Y.Z-sqd.N is built from ponder@X.Y.Z + the Portal layer (rev N). The ponder version stays visible; bump `-sqd.<rev>` for a fork-side fix on the SAME ponder version (npm permanently retires an unpublished version number, so a plain mirror like 0.16.6 can't be re-cut after a bad publish). The NEWEST ponder version is published with `--tag latest` (the default `npm install`); an older version publishes under a `ponder-<version>` dist-tag instead of clobbering `latest`. The bin stays `ponder` (drop-in). We cut a release only for ponder versions a client needs; `compat.tested` records which versions the seam is proven against.

0.17.3-sqd.1 grafts the current Portal layer onto ponder@0.17.3. wiring/0.17.3.patch is a VERBATIM copy of wiring/0.17.2.patch (sha256 23ad65db…, same 12 files) — the verbatim lineage now runs 0.17.0→0.17.1→0.17.2→0.17.3, one patch throughout. 0.17.2→0.17.3 is ONE upstream PATCH-level bugfix, ponder-sh/ponder#2350 (commit 80dd936, @kyscott18): 'Fixed a bug that caused realtime sync to retain unfiltered block transactions in memory until finalization. Memory usage for live indexing improved >10%.' The ENTIRE source delta in packages/core/src is one line in src/sync-realtime/index.ts, inside the reconcileBlock async generator (~L1140): `blockWithEventData.block.transactions = blockWithFilteredEventData.transactions` — previously `… = blockWithFilteredEventData.block.transactions`, a self-assignment (A = A) no-op that left the block's own transactions array pointing at the UNFILTERED set and thus un-GC-able; the fix repoints it at the already-filtered top-level `transactions` array so the unfiltered array is released. (A test-only change to src/sync-realtime/index.test.ts is not grafted.) sync-realtime/index.ts IS one of the 12 wiring files, BUT the #2350 edit at ~L1140 does NOT overlap the wiring patch's two hunks (the import block @L31 and the #23 filtered-logs shouldRequestLogs fallback @L308-347): the 0.17.2 patch applies to ponder@0.17.3 with ZERO rejects — all 12 files 'Applied … cleanly', the shouldRequestLogs hunk landing at 313 with the same +3-line offset carried since 0.17.2 (the two #2347 additions above it, unchanged in 0.17.3). RISK REVIEWED AND EMPIRICALLY REFUTED (candor): a review seat flagged that the change moves the yielded block's `block.transactions` from the unfiltered to the filtered set, so any consumer reading `yieldedBlock.block.transactions` expecting the FULL set (e.g. realtime access_list preservation, issue #27) would silently see fewer txs. Verified: (a) the `block.transactions` reads that exist in stock core — rpc/actions.ts RPC-response validation and the sync-realtime fetch/assembly (~L677) — all run UPSTREAM of the reassignment, on the RAW fetched block during fetch→validate→filter, never on the post-reassignment/yielded block; the L1140 site is the sole writer and no consumer of the yielded realtime event reads `event.block.transactions` (runtime/events.ts builds the indexed event from block header fields plus the top-level filtered `transactions`); (b) realtime transactions are persisted via insertTransactions from the TOP-LEVEL `transactions` field (filtered, byte-identical logic in 0.17.2 and 0.17.3), never from `block.transactions`; (c) the Portal layer reads only its own Portal-shaped blocks (b.transactions with b.header.number) and top-level ev.transactions/batch.transactions — never ponder's post-filter `yieldedBlock.block.transactions`. So the change persists NO different data on either the RPC or Portal /stream path; it only frees memory (and incidentally makes block.transactions consistent with the indexed filtered set). Inherited VERBATIM from upstream — not a Portal-side or wiring-introduced behavior change. supportedLines.policy: A SUPPORTED LINE is a ponder version we advertise a moving dist-tag for: the newest (`latest`) plus each `ponder-<version>` tag. The Portal layer is version-agnostic, so every supported line CAN carry the same layer — and this policy is what keeps them in sync. GOING FORWARD, every fork-side fix release (any `-sqd.<rev>` bump on `latest`) TRIGGERS a backport wave: the same portal layer is rev-bumped and re-published on every other supported line, each gated identically (`scripts/sync-upstream.sh <ver> --test` full suite green per version). A per-version gate failure surfaces to a human — never ship a red line, never silently skip one. Dropping a line from support is an explicit change here + a README note (never silent staleness). Pin-exact historical builds (versions with no moving dist-tag) are frozen and are NOT backported. NOTE (2026-07-28): the catch-up wave has LANDED — every supported line now carries the current Portal layer, built from the same portal/ tree: latest `0.17.2-sqd.1`, `ponder-0.16.10`→`0.16.10-sqd.2`, `ponder-0.16.6`→`0.16.6-sqd.3`, `ponder-0.15.17`→`0.15.17-sqd.3` (all published 2026-07-28, each gated green by `scripts/sync-upstream.sh <ver> --test`). Going forward this policy keeps them in lockstep.
